actions.justification: Mandatory first step to establish baseline hemodynamic status and confirm stability in a patient presenting with palpitations and dizziness.
Mandatory diagnostic test to identify the underlying cardiac rhythm (e.g., atrial fibrillation, flutter, SVT) causing palpitations and dizziness.
Mandatory risk stratification tool for stroke risk in suspected atrial fibrillation; patient has hypertension which contributes to the score.
Mandatory lab - BMP evaluates electrolytes (K+, Mg, Ca) and renal function, which are critical in arrhythmia workup and guide safe medication use.
Mandatory lab - TSH screens for hyperthyroidism, a common reversible cause of atrial fibrillation and palpitations.
Patient presenting with palpitations and dizziness requires continuous cardiac monitoring to detect arrhythmia recurrence, rate changes, or hemodynamic instability while awaiting lab results.
CHA2DS2-VASc score has been assessed; now formally evaluate anticoagulation need based on the score, patient's hypertension history, and clinical presentation to guide treatment decisions.

Patient with palpitations, dizziness, and hypertension likely has an arrhythmia (possibly AFib). Cardiology consultation is indicated to guide rate/rhythm control strategy and further management after initial assessment and ECG are reviewed.

Patient presenting with palpitations and dizziness with history of hypertension. Cardiology already consulted; electrophysiology consult is warranted to evaluate for underlying arrhythmia etiology (e.g., atrial fibrillation, SVT, WPW) and guide further management after ECG review.

If ECG confirms atrial fibrillation or other tachyarrhythmia requiring rate control, initiating rate control therapy is appropriate. Current HR is 80 bpm which is controlled, but this action prepares for rhythm-guided management per guideline. Assess ECG findings first.
Patient reports dizziness; IV fluid support may help if there is a component of volume depletion or vagal response contributing to symptoms, supporting hemodynamic stability during workup.

Order a repeat/formal ECG to assess current cardiac rhythm given palpitations and dizziness — supports rhythm characterization beyond the initial 12-lead if rhythm has changed or to document current status.
Chest X-ray is indicated to evaluate for cardiomegaly, pulmonary edema, or other structural causes contributing to palpitations in a hypertensive patient.
Echocardiogram is recommended to assess for structural heart disease, valvular pathology, or left atrial enlargement which may be contributing to the arrhythmia in this hypertensive patient.
CBC to evaluate for anemia, infection, or other hematologic causes contributing to palpitations and dizziness in this hypertensive patient.
Coagulation studies (PT/INR) are needed to assess baseline coagulation status before considering anticoagulation therapy, especially relevant if atrial fibrillation is suspected.

Echocardiogram to evaluate cardiac structure and function, assess for structural heart disease, left atrial size, and ventricular function which guides management of arrhythmia in this hypertensive patient with palpitations.

Renal function assessment is important for anticoagulation dosing decisions (e.g., DOAC dosing) and to evaluate for renal causes or complications in this patient with hypertension presenting with palpitations/dizziness.

INR is needed to assess coagulation status and guide anticoagulation decisions for possible atrial fibrillation, especially if warfarin is being considered or patient has been on prior anticoagulation.
Lactate helps rule out hemodynamic compromise or end-organ hypoperfusion, which is relevant given the chief complaint of dizziness alongside palpitations.
Troponin should be ordered to rule out myocardial injury/ACS as a cause of palpitations and to assess for tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy, especially relevant given the cardiac presentation.
NT-proBNP helps assess for heart failure as a contributing factor to palpitations and dizziness, and provides prognostic information in atrial fibrillation management.

Patient with palpitations and dizziness, likely atrial fibrillation given the workup completed. CHA2DS2-VASc assessment has been done and anticoagulation need assessed. Initiating anticoagulation is appropriate to reduce thromboembolic risk, especially with hypertension as a comorbidity contributing to stroke risk score.

Beta blocker therapy for rate control in likely atrial fibrillation. Current HR is 80 which is reasonable, but beta blocker may have been the rate control agent already given or may need titration for symptom management and rate control maintenance.
